summary_oneline: A legal LLM Wiki fits ai-parrot's knowledge stack far better than the source assumed — the legal vocabulary, the deterministic traversals, the incremental sync and the read-only guarantee are all existing declarative machinery — but two of its stated 'closed' decisions are refuted, temporal validity remains wholly greenfield, and a parallel feature (FEAT-450) is already building the multi-brain layer it needs.

constraints.statement: GraphIndex has no namespace concept; the only isolation unit is TenantContext, which allocates a separate ArangoDB database (and pgvector schema) per tenant
constraints.implication: The source's OQ1 'Closed: single Arango DB, GraphIndex namespaces over shared collections, tenancy as a second discriminator' is not implementable as written. Either legal materias become tenants (one DB each, inverting the OQ1 decision), or a namespace discriminator is new framework work.

constraints.statement: The graph entity/edge vocabulary is declarative YAML merged per tenant, with auto-provisioning of Arango collections and a shipped domain example
constraints.implication: The legal collections (norma, articulo, sentencia, modifica, deroga, cita...) are configuration, not a GraphIndex fork. This is the single largest de-risking of the design.

constraints.statement: No temporal-validity machinery exists anywhere in parrot/knowledge/ (2 grep hits, both unrelated)
constraints.implication: versions[], article_in_force(as_of), per-version chunks and as_of-filtered vector retrieval are entirely new, with no pattern to copy. This is the design's hardest component and its correctness gate.

constraints.statement: The TOOL_CALL guardrail seam exists and runs first inside ToolManager.execute_tool, but zero counting/rate-limiting guardrails ship
constraints.implication: Code-enforced CENDOJ budgets are achievable as a new Guardrail subclass on an existing extension point — small, well-bounded new work, not a ToolManager change.

constraints.statement: A grounded, read-only, citation-audited advisory agent already exists end-to-end in agents/security_advisor.py, including a citation re-audit that gates automated action
constraints.implication: LegalAnswerAgent and the verified/pending_verification gate should extend a proven pattern rather than be designed fresh; note agents/ is gitignored and needs git add -f.

constraints.statement: The @schedule decorator lives in the ai-parrot-server[scheduler] satellite, reachable from core only via a lazy __getattr__ shim
constraints.implication: Daily BOE/EUR-Lex sync implies an ai-parrot-server dependency or an external scheduler calling an ingestion entrypoint; the spec must say which.

constraints.statement: parrot.interfaces is documented as a mixins package for bot functionality, not a home for domain data models
constraints.implication: CaseRef/CendojVerification/LegalAnswer belong in the toolkit tree (the source's own parrot_tools/legal/... layout), not at parrot.interfaces.legal.

constraints.statement: No legal-domain code exists in the repo; the commit titled 'new tooling for legal resources' added only the design document
constraints.implication: Nothing to reconcile or migrate — but also no partial head start, so every sprint in the roadmap is from zero.

constraints.statement: The repo's only CircuitBreaker is embedded in the compression codec latency router; there is no shared throttled HTTP client abstraction
constraints.implication: The CENDOJ shared client (semaphore pacing, Retry-After, 15-min breaker) is new infrastructure with one class worth studying, not inheriting.

constraints.statement: FEAT-450 wiki-namespaces is a live parallel proposal whose stated goal explicitly includes composing a lawyer's legislation/jurisprudence/own-cases brains behind ns::id routing, with an arangodb namespace kind keyed by database
constraints.implication: The brain-federation half of U1 is being solved concurrently. This feature should consume FEAT-450 rather than design its own multiplicity scheme — and should coordinate, since FEAT-450 v1 defers the intent-based router that the legal design's 4.1 assumes.

constraints.statement: The wiki plane models pages and categories, not typed entities, but its ingest orchestrator already mirrors nodes into GraphIndex via sync_graph=True
constraints.implication: A layered answer is available: wiki namespaces for brain selection and document ingest, GraphIndex+Ontology beneath for the typed legal graph. These are complementary, not a fork.

constraints.statement: Collections can be added to a live tenant idempotently via ensure_collection, and tenant database naming is a configurable template with overlay support
constraints.implication: Choosing tenant-per-materia is reversible and incremental; the 'wrong choice means migrate everything' fear is materially weaker than assumed.

constraints.statement: A six-stage CRON delta-sync pipeline already exists at the ontology layer (EXTRACT/DIFF/APPLY with soft-delete/REDISCOVER/SYNC embeddings/INVALIDATE)
constraints.implication: boe_sync_consolidated(since) and the daily incremental sync are largely configuration of existing machinery, not new infrastructure.

constraints.statement: TraversalPattern expresses a named AQL template with bind variables, keyword fast-path triggers, declarative authorization and a post-traversal tool_call, loadable from ontology overlays
constraints.implication: The deterministic traversals in 3.4 become declarative config with as_of as a bind variable, and the CENDOJ verification step has a native hook — removing the query layer from the greenfield column.

constraints.statement: Graph queries are validated read-only at the AQL layer: mutations, system collections and JavaScript are rejected
constraints.implication: The read-only-agent invariant is enforced below the tool layer, so the source's separate writer/reader toolkit split may be unnecessary ceremony.

constraints.statement: There are two distinct write paths — GraphIndexBuilder writing UniversalNodes under a closed NodeKind enum, and the ontology EntityDef path writing arbitrary typed collections
constraints.implication: Typed legal entities require the ontology path, but the loader/embedding/incremental-refresh pipeline lives on the GraphIndex path. Reconciling the two is a design decision the source never considered and is now the sharpest open technical question.

risks.risk: Two incompatible write paths — GraphIndexBuilder's closed NodeKind enum vs the ontology's arbitrary typed collections — and the loader/embedding/incremental pipeline sits on the wrong one for typed legal entities
The temporal-validity DATA MODEL remains entirely greenfield and is the design's correctness gate; the EUR-Lex half rests on a diff-derived approximation the source itself flags as derived=true
CENDOJ is the only verification path for Spanish ordinary case law and is an unsanctioned scrape with a captcha/429 posture; if unusable, the verified tier collapses to commercial backends or nothing
FEAT-450 is building the multi-brain layer concurrently and defers the intent router this design depends on; uncoordinated, the two features will duplicate or contradict each other
A five-sprint roadmap with two blocking spikes is far past what a single spec should carry

unknowns.question: Given that FEAT-450 is already building wiki namespaces for exactly this multi-brain case (F014) and that typed legal entities need the ontology write path rather than the GraphIndex one (F020,C21), what is the substrate split?
plausible_answers: Layered: FEAT-450 wiki namespaces for brain selection and document ingest, one ontology tenant per materia beneath for the typed legal graph — uses existing machinery on both levels and makes this feature depend on FEAT-450
Single ontology tenant, materia as a node property and edge filter, no wiki namespaces — simplest and independent of FEAT-450, but no hard isolation between domains
Add a namespace discriminator to GraphIndex itself — matches the source's OQ1 as written but is new core work that likely duplicates FEAT-450
unknowns.user_answer: Layered: FEAT-450 wiki namespaces for brain selection and document ingest, with one ontology tenant per materia beneath carrying the typed legal graph. This inverts the source's OQ1 — isolation is a database per materia, not namespaces over shared collections.

unknowns.question: Should this feature block on FEAT-450, or proceed independently and integrate later?

Proceed independently on the typed graph (ontology tenant) and integrate namespaces when FEAT-450 lands
Merge the two efforts and treat the legal wiki as FEAT-450's first real consumer
unknowns.user_answer: Proceed independently and integrate later. Build the typed legal graph on an ontology tenant now; adopt namespace routing when FEAT-450 lands. The integration seam is the wiki ingest sync_graph bridge.

recommended_next_command.rationale: All five unknowns are resolved and v1 is now scoped to a single self-contained deliverable (BOE norms graph, zero LLM) whose substrate, sequencing and deployment are all decided — the architectural fork that argued for brainstorming has been closed by D1 and D2.

meta.notes: Two research rounds; round two added at user request (FEAT-450 overlap, tenant provisioning/migration, AQL surface, ingestion path). Net effect: the design is MORE feasible than round one suggested — legal collections, traversals, incremental sync and read-only enforcement are all existing declarative machinery — while two risks sharpened: the GraphIndex-vs-ontology write-path split (new, C21) and the concurrent FEAT-450 overlap (C16). Temporal validity remains the one genuinely greenfield component. Phase 5 resolved all five unknowns (D1-D5), collapsing the architectural fork and narrowing v1 from a five-sprint roadmap to Sprint 1 only; recommendation moved from sdd-brainstorm to sdd-spec.
